transcript.text: Every morning I open our AP inbox. Invoices come in from about forty vendors, and honestly no two look alike. Most are PDFs, some are just photos, and a few vendors paste the invoice right into the email body.

First I open the email and download the attachment. If there is no attachment I check whether the invoice is in the body. When I see it is from Meridian, I know the second page is just their terms, so I ignore it.

Then I pull out the vendor name, invoice number, amount, and due date, and I key those into our tracking spreadsheet. Usually the amount is on the first page, but for freight invoices it is at the bottom of page two.

Next I check the PO number in NetSuite. I search by vendor and match the amount. If the amounts do not match exactly I flag it. Anything over five hundred dollars has to go to Sarah for sign-off before I can enter it.
Once it matches, I create the bill in NetSuite: vendor, invoice number, amount, due date, and the GL code. Office supplies go to 6200, freight goes to 6450. If I am not sure, I ask in the AP channel.

Finally I reply to the vendor confirming we received it and it is scheduled, then I drag the email into the Processed folder. If something is wrong, missing PO or a weird amount, I reply asking for a corrected invoice instead.
